claims.text: Under dynamic tensile loading, single-crystalline <110>-oriented CoCrFeNi nanopillars undergo deformation-induced reordering of local chemical order.
The deformation-induced local chemical reordering occurs rapidly.
Reordering of local chemical order lowers the local stacking-fault energy.
Lower local stacking-fault energy promotes the combined activation of dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
Combined dislocation slip and deformation twinning cause higher strength and ductility under dynamic loading than under quasi-static loading.
The initial CoCrFeNi nanopillars have homogeneous chemical order and uniform microstructural characteristics.
High-strain-rate loading produces localized regions with reduced stacking-fault energy.
Concurrent slip and twinning distribute plasticity more uniformly.
More uniform plasticity delays necking.
Dynamic tests will produce a higher twin-boundary density than quasi-static tests.
Dynamic tests will produce measurable diffraction or spectroscopic shifts associated with local chemical-order evolution.
Local chemical-order changes and increased twin density will correlate with higher uniform elongation and flow stress.
At strain rates below the activation regime, local chemical-order reordering and twin formation will be minimal or absent.
Quasi-static tests exhibit minimal local chemical-order evolution and fewer twins than dynamic tests.
Quasi-static tests exhibit lower work hardening and uniform elongation than dynamic tests.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to sufficiently high strain rates in single-crystalline <110>-oriented CoCrFeNi nanopillars at room temperature.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to polycrystalline specimens or substantially different temperatures.
Specimen size and preparation may affect the strain-rate threshold and measured response.
A strain-rate series with otherwise matched nanopillars can test whether local chemical-order evolution, twin density, and mechanical response change together.

The mechanism would be falsified if dynamic and quasi-static tests show no significant difference in twin density or local chemical ordering, or if mechanical enhancements do not correlate with those microstructural changes.
